title: Daily Stretching to Improve Walking in Older Patients With Peripheral Artery Disease: The STRETCH PAD Study
official: Daily Stretching to Improve Walking and Calf Muscle Function in Older Patients With Peripheral Artery Disease: The STRETCH PAD Study
summary:
The goal of this multi-center clinical trial is to assess the effects of passive calf muscle stretching in older adults diagnosed with peripheral artery disease (PAD). The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. To determine how calf muscle stretching at home affects treadmill walk performance and daily physical activity level after 4 weeks and 6 months in these patients.
2. To determine how calf muscle stretching at home affects calf muscle vascular function and walking gait.

Participants will use inflatable ankle stretch boots for 30 minutes a day, 5 days a week for 4-weeks
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adult male or female. Women must not be pregnant, nor plan to become pregnant or be breast feeding
* Agree to participate voluntarily and sign an IRB approved consent form.
* ≥50 years of age
* Individuals with peripheral artery disease. Objective evidence of PAD: ankle brachial index (ABI)\<0.9 at rest; or any other diagnostic test confirming PAD including but not limited to hemodynamic or imaging modalities confirming PAD.
* PAD presentation or symptomatology consistent with Fontaine Stage IIa or IIb (intermittent claudication pain).
* PAD symptoms must be stable for at least 3 months to exclude acute thrombotic events.
* A peak walking time (PWT) \< 360 seconds on a graded 6-minutes treadmill walking protocol

Exclusion Criteria:

* Terminal illness (\<12-month life expectancy)
* Inability to provide inform consent
* Uncontrolled arrhythmias
* Inability to cooperate during exams
* Significant infection or inflammation
* Currently engaged in a structured, organized, and supervised physical training program
* Enrolled in an interventional trial on PAD
* Scheduled to undergo revascularization or major elective surgery within the next 6 months
* Current critical limb ischemia or above/below-knee amputation, wheelchair-bound, or requires the use of a walker or cane
* Underwent lower extremity revascularization, or coronary artery bypass surgery within 3 months of screening
* Underwent major orthopedic surgery within 6 months of screening
* End stage renal disease (requiring dialysis)
* Significant hepatic dysfunction (AST and/or ALT \>5xULN, bilirubin \>2xULN)
* Parkinson's disease
* Recent history of alcohol or drug abuse
* Inability to walk on a treadmill
* Advanced heart failure: New York Heart Association (NYHA) class III or IV, or last known left ventricular ejection fraction \< 30%),
* Severe or very severe COPD (forced expiratory volume (FEV-1) ≤ 50%)
* Severe pulmonary condition that requires oxygen
* Resting SpO₂ ≤92% or ≥4% desaturation with exercise
* ≥1 mm ST depression/elevation (abnormal ECG finding)
